title: World as a System
lines: World as a System turns school subjects into small, inspectable reasoning models.
Its thousand problems supply facts, rules, and questions across four primary-school grades.
The task is to explain why an answer follows, rather than guess a plausible result.

title: Two moves east
lines: Imagine one town east of another, and a third town one step farther east.
Composing the two moves makes the relationship visible.
An irrelevant museum fact changes no coordinate, giving children a simple test of relevance.

title: Different subjects, shared habits
lines: Later tasks combine route constraints, historical evidence, civic rules, and environmental flows.
A majority may still fail a stated quorum; a renewable resource can still be depleted.
The same habit is to keep every relevant condition visible before concluding.

title: Work through the model
lines: Read it with a learner to compare reasoning steps, not just final answers.
Begin with a short chain, then vary one condition and recompute the result.
The worked solutions provide models to test and discuss, rather than an infallible answer key.
